Description: Creates a new Business record in DB. Simple businessModel.create().
Criticality Reason: Business profile creation is a foundational operation — businesses are the root entity for representatives and customers. Unprotected endpoint allows anyone to create business records.
Sensitive Data: registrationNumber (business TIN) in request and response.
Dependencies: DB: Business.create (Sequelize/MSSQL).
Existing Observability: None. No logging in handler or service method.
Observability Gap: SECURITY: Endpoint is completely unprotected — no authentication, no authorization. Zero logging. Zero metrics. Zero tracing.
Notes: SECURITY CRITICAL: No @UseGuards() decorator. Anyone can create business records. Must add AccessGuard immediately.

Dependencies: DB: Business.findAndCountAll with Representative include (Sequelize/MSSQL). HTTP: Access Management Service (guard).
Observability Gap: No structured logging. Error logging is bare console.error with no context.

Observability Gap: SECURITY: Guard is commented out — endpoint exposes PII without authentication. Zero logging. Zero metrics.
Notes: SECURITY CRITICAL: @UseGuards(AccessGuard) is commented out. Exposes business + representative PII to anyone. Must re-enable guard.

Description: Despite appearing to be a local DB lookup, makes TWO external HTTP calls to Access Control Service: (1) POST /api/auth/login with hardcoded credentials, (2) POST /api/access/rdb/company-profile with {tin: id} to fetch from government registry (RDB). Formats response with registration info, representative, shareholders, board members.
Criticality Reason: Integrates with external government registry (RDB). Contains hardcoded service credentials. Returns extensive PII of shareholders and board members. Failure or latency in external service directly impacts user experience. Credential exposure is a security risk.
Sensitive Data: CRITICAL: ACCESS_CON_USER and ACCESS_CON_PASSWORD sent in plaintext body to external service. Response contains extensive PII: full names, dates of birth, nationality, gender, identity document numbers, phone numbers, emails, physical addresses of shareholders and board members.
Dependencies: External HTTP: Access Control Service (2 calls — login + company-profile). HTTP: Access Management Service (guard). NO local DB query.
Observability Gap: Zero logging on external API calls. No latency tracking on government registry integration. No error handling metrics. Hardcoded credentials sent in plaintext.
Notes: SECURITY CRITICAL: Hardcoded service credentials (ACCESS_CON_USER, ACCESS_CON_PASSWORD) sent in plaintext POST body. External API failure is invisible. Must add structured logging with latency + error tracking. Consider credential vault.

Criticality Reason: Business documents are compliance-critical (registration certificates, tax clearances, licenses). File upload + DB record creation. Validates before uploading to avoid storage waste on duplicates.
Sensitive Data: JWT token. Document files may contain sensitive business information. FILE_SERVER_AUTHORIZATION sent to file server.
Dependencies: DB: Business.findOne (validate), BusinessDocument.findOne (dup check per doc), BusinessDocument.create (Sequelize/MSSQL). External HTTP: File server (multipart upload). HTTP: Access Management Service (guard).
Observability Gap: Zero logging. Zero metrics. File upload to external server is invisible. Duplicate check is per-document in loop (no batch).
Notes: Validates before upload (good pattern). JSON.parse of payload.documents may throw if malformed — no specific error handling.

Observability Gap: SECURITY: Endpoint completely unprotected — accepts extensive PII without authentication. console.log may leak PII to stdout. No structured logging. No metrics.

Description: Handles composite business-owner creation event. Creates Business + Representative + Customer in a single Sequelize transaction. Idempotent — checks for existing records by registrationNumber/identificationNumber/customerId before creating.
Criticality Reason: Creates the foundational entity chain (Business → Representative → Customer) for business onboarding. Transaction failure leaves the business partially created. All downstream services depend on these records existing.
Sensitive Data: Extensive PII in payload: business registration number, representative identificationNumber/fullName/phone/email, customer identificationNumber/dateOfBirth/income/address.
Dependencies: DB: Business.findOne + Business.create, Representative.findOne + Representative.create, Customer.findOne + Customer.create — all in transaction (Sequelize/MSSQL).
Existing Observability: console.log on event receipt + on skipping + on each entity creation. console.error on failure.
Observability Gap: console.log is unstructured and may leak PII. No metrics on event processing rate/latency. No dead-letter queue on failure. No correlation ID from source event.
Notes: Most critical Kafka handler — creates the entire business entity chain. console.log statements likely log PII (identificationNumber, phone, email). Must replace with structured SDK logging with PII redaction.

Description: Creates individual customer from Kafka event. Idempotent (checks email/identificationNumber). Resolves businessId from registration number.
Criticality Reason: Customer creation from external events. Race condition: if this event arrives before user.created, customer is created without business association (businessId = undefined). No retry mechanism.
Sensitive Data: Full customer PII in payload: identificationNumber, dateOfBirth, income, email, phone, address.
Dependencies: DB: Customer.findOne (dup check), Business.findOne (resolve businessId), Customer.create (Sequelize/MSSQL).
Existing Observability: console.log on event receipt and successful creation. console.error on failure.
Observability Gap: Unstructured console.log may leak PII. No metrics. RACE CONDITION: if business not yet created, customer loses business association permanently — no retry, no DLQ.
Notes: Race condition with user.created event ordering. If business creation event hasn't been processed, customer is created without businessId and no mechanism exists to fix this later.

Description: Creates representative from Kafka event. Requires businessId (actually registrationNumber). Looks up business by registrationNumber. If business not found — SILENTLY SKIPS creation entirely. No retry. Representative is permanently lost.
Criticality Reason: Silent data loss: if business hasn't been created yet, the representative is permanently lost. No retry mechanism, no dead-letter queue, no compensation event. The representative will never be created.
Sensitive Data: Representative PII: identificationNumber (national ID), fullName, phone, email.
Dependencies: DB: Business.findOne (resolve business), Representative.findOne (dup check), Representative.create (Sequelize/MSSQL).
Existing Observability: console.log on event receipt + business lookup result + creation. console.warn when business not found (skipping). console.error on failure.
Observability Gap: CRITICAL DATA LOSS RISK: Silent skip when business not found. console.warn logs the skip but no alert, no retry, no DLQ. Unstructured logging may leak PII.
Notes: CRITICAL: Representative is permanently lost if business creation event hasn't been processed yet. Must implement retry with backoff or dead-letter queue. console.warn is insufficient — needs structured alert-level logging + metric for monitoring.
